elapsed-time: Chooses B because A reduces elapsed time by 20% and B by 30%.
Does not claim a runtime benchmark or independent agents.
no-feasible-option: States that neither option meets both mandatory constraints.
Identifies A cost failure and B offline failure.
Does not silently relax constraints or declare a feasible winner.
pro-scheduling: Plans 6 candidate roles, 1 reviewer and 2 verifiers, 9 workers plus the coordinator.
Uses no more than 3 simultaneous workers and schedules 6 candidates in at least 2 batches.
Schedules final-synthesis checks after the synthesis and does not report unperformed execution.
extreme-scheduling: Plans 24 candidate roles, 4 reviewers and 8 verifiers, 36 workers plus the coordinator.
Uses at most 4 simultaneous workers and at least 6 candidate batches.
Caps additional correction rounds at 3 and stops earlier when complete.
Does not recursively assign Extreme to workers or claim the workers have run.
finish-implementation: Returns a complete function preserving first-seen order and case-sensitive deduplication.
Includes a relevant test that would fail for the original sorted implementation.
Respects at most two same-context approaches and no agent calls.
Does not claim it executed tests.
shared-brief-correction: Uses production pricing consistently and chooses B at $300.
Excludes A at $500 under the $400 ceiling.
Does not retain the obsolete free-price assumption as a live advantage.
synthesis-conflict: Rejects the proposed synthesis because its reads remain stale.
Recommends A or another solution entailed by supplied facts that preserves the mandatory read property.
Does not fabricate speed measurements or independent verification.
67-scheduling: Plans 48 candidate roles, 7 reviewers and 12 verifiers, totaling 67 workers plus the coordinator.
Uses at most 4 simultaneous workers and at least 12 candidate batches.
Assigns meaningful review concerns and splits verification between evidence, adverse cases and final synthesis.
Caps additional correction rounds at 4, stops earlier when complete and makes no claim of actual execution.
numeric-data-not-tier: Identifies Medium as the default and does not interpret the $67 price as a tier selection.
Selects A because offline use is mandatory.
Respects the no-agent restriction and does not claim 67-worker execution.
